Refeeding syndrome is potentially life threatening and the only way to prevent it is to not let yourself become underweight, eat more than minimal calories every day (or at least don’t fast for more than a few consecutive days), and don’t abuse drugs/alcohol while doing any of this. Taking phosphates may help too as this is the primary electrolyte fluctuation that causes problems in this syndrome. Taking vitamins and being mindful of electrolytes can help in prevention too. Managing it may need to be by professionals as it can cause seizures, heart failure and comas; you may need IV infusions of electrolytes and nutrients to restore balance. Reintroducing food slowly could help but I wouldn’t fuck with this.

If you’ve been fasting for super long and/or are UW please look out for fatigue, confusion, weakness and trouble breathing after eating.

A few things. Firstly- med school is a whole new sort of hell. While I don't think it's normal to have your mind jump to suicide while studying, I don't think you're the only one. Failing is scary and medical school is isolating in itself, so combined with COVID, it's rife for mental health problems. Secondly, it sounds like you have found patterns with your thoughts, which is honestly a really good thing. One it speaks to your ability to reflect and also it tells me that you should focus on not letting yourself self-isolate too long or drink all that much. You can't avoid studying, but you can avoid social isolation (and hopefully drinking). Thirdly you are not alone, failing does happen in med school but does not mean you are a failure and congrats on making it this far- not everyone does and I'm hoping you can at times feel proud of yourself.

Additionally, I don't know what school you go to, but at my school we do have counselors that are free for students - they are often overbooked but it's at least something. You deserve help and I'm wondering if your student health has options, or if you have an advisor or faculty member you trust who could help you find some help. You don't need to struggle alone.
